## Understanding the Power of Clinic Design
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/understanding-the-power-of-clinic-design/

In today’s highly competitive healthcare environment, understanding the power of design within your clinic is more important than ever. A well-thought-out design goes beyond aesthetics; it plays a critical role in enhancing patient experience, improving workflow efficiency, and even boosting staff morale. Designing a clinic is a delicate balancing act that requires a thoughtful blend of patient comfort and business efficiency.
When patients enter a clinic that is welcoming, clean, and thoughtfully organized, it immediately sets a tone of professionalism and care. This can significantly reduce anxiety and create a comforting atmosphere, which is particularly important in a medical setting where patients may already be feeling vulnerable. Patient comfort is paramount because it directly impacts the overall experience, satisfaction, and even the recovery process. When patients feel at ease, they are more likely to trust their healthcare providers, adhere to treatment plans, and return for follow-up visits. Elements like soothing colour schemes, comfortable seating, and private spaces for consultations can significantly enhance comfort levels, making the clinic a welcoming environment for everyone.
On the other hand, business efficiency cannot be overlooked. An efficiently run clinic ensures that resources are used wisely, reducing wait times and improving the workflow for healthcare providers. This efficiency translates into better patient care, as medical professionals can focus more on their patients rather than administrative hurdles. Efficient design elements might include streamlined check-in processes, strategically placed examination rooms to reduce walking distances for staff, and digital record-keeping systems to minimize paperwork. Moreover, a functional design can streamline operations, reducing bottlenecks and improving the overall flow of both patients and staff. For instance, strategically placed examination rooms and administrative areas can minimize unnecessary walking and waiting times, allowing healthcare providers to deliver quicker and more efficient care. This not only increases patient satisfaction but also maximizes the clinic’s capacity to see more patients in a day without compromising on quality.
Additionally, the design of a clinic can have a profound impact on staff well-being. A thoughtfully designed workspace that includes ergonomic furniture, natural lighting, and designated break areas can greatly enhance staff comfort and productivity. Happy staff are more likely to provide better care, creating a positive cycle that benefits everyone involved.
The key to successful clinic design lies in harmonizing these aspects. For instance, an open-plan layout might boost efficiency by facilitating better communication among staff, but it should also incorporate soundproofing and private areas to maintain patient comfort. Similarly, advanced scheduling software can optimize appointment times, but it should also be user-friendly and accessible to patients of all ages and tech-savviness.
Ultimately, investing in a good design for your clinic is not just about making the space look appealing; it’s about creating an environment that promotes healing, efficiency, and well-being. With careful planning and consideration, the design of your clinic can be a powerful tool in delivering exceptional healthcare. A clinic that marries patient comfort with business efficiency not only stands to improve health outcomes but also enhances its reputation and operational longevity. Patients will appreciate the thoughtful environment, and staff will benefit from a well-organized workspace, creating a thrive-able space for your patients, staff and your business.
To learn more about what a GREAT design can do for your clinic, book a discovery call with our team here!

## Veterinary Clinic Construction & Design
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/veterinary-clinic-construction/


## Top Tips for Designing Veterinary Clinic in Canada
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/veterinary-clinic-in-canada/

Designing a veterinary clinic in Canada requires specialized knowledge to ensure compliance with local, provincial, and national regulations. It’s essential to create a visually appealing space that blends comfort, innovation, and functionality. However, when designing layouts for a veterinary practice, architects and designers must balance the needs of doctors and staff with the requirement to maintain a hygienic and safe environment for both animal patients and the humans who care for them.
Team Medico had the pleasure in doing the interior design for multiple veterinary clinics. If you’re in the process of designing a veterinary clinic or seeking to enhance your practice’s current workspace, we have valuable interior design tips to assist you in creating a cutting-edge veterinary clinic. These suggestions will help you optimize the functionality, aesthetics, and efficiency of your clinic, providing a state-of-the-art environment for both your animal patients and your veterinary team.
#### Comfortable Waiting Room
A comfortable waiting room and reception area are crucial components of a veterinary clinic in Canada. These are the first areas that clients and their pets encounter when they visit your clinic. Creating a welcoming and comfortable environment immediately sets a positive tone and helps establish a favorable first impression. Animals visiting the clinic may experience stress and anxiety due to unfamiliar surroundings or medical procedures. A comfortable waiting room with soothing colors, soft lighting, comfortable seating, and a calming ambiance can help alleviate these feelings, creating a more relaxed atmosphere for both pets and their owners.
#### Functional Layout & Design
A well-planned layout for a veterinary clinic in Canada maximizes the use of available space, improves workflow, and helps create a clutter-free environment. It considers the logical flow of patients, staff, and supplies, minimizing unnecessary movements and reducing the risk of errors or delays. A functional design allows for seamless transitions between different areas, such as the waiting room, examination rooms, and treatment areas, promoting optimal productivity. To ensure the well-being and safety of animals undergoing surgery, it is recommended to avoid locating surgery rooms on higher floors if kennel or holding areas are situated downstairs.
Select a qualified construction contractor who has experience in designing Veterinary clinics. The qualified & experienced specialist will help navigate the intricate details of Vet Clinic design including:
- Finishes – Type of floors (anti-slip floors), fixtures, paints, countertops to choose for easy cleaning and maintenance. Epoxy flooring throughout the clinic is great for its non-absorbent and impermeable abilities, as well as its high durability and resistance to chemical cleaning and daily wear and tear. Read more about modern and contemporary Vet Hospital we designed for our client E.P.I.C Veterinary Hospital, Richmond, BC
- A well-constructed holding area to prevent animals from getting injured or escape
- Dedicated space for cold storage / refrigeration.
- Create a warm and welcoming environment with lot of natural lighting.
- Lockup facilities to safely keep medical equipment.
- Details of equipment including power, ventilation and safety of X-rays.
#### Safety & Hygiene Considerations
Sustainable design, safety & hygiene is a top priority when designing Vet Clinic. A well-designed space should have enough space to move around between different areas. A thoughtfully designed floor plan should not only secure the premises for the drugs and equipment but also prevent pets from escaping.
Noise from Vet Clinic can be extremely troublesome for the pet owners, vet clinic staff and of course the pets. Acoustic panels between walls and acoustic doors can help to control noise levels.
To prevent unpleasant odours, the entire structure must be zoned with several independent heating and air conditioning systems, each with its own air supply and return; some of these exhaust air to the outdoors. For instance, we don’t want exhausted air to be pumped back through the building in isolation rooms or hospital wards where it can be contaminated by odour or illness.
#### State-of-the-art Equipment
As a veterinary hospital, you are expected to provide high-level and advanced care. It’s important to have the right tools for the job to provide quality care. Here are some pieces of equipment that are essential for any vet clinic such as Blood count Analyzer, Biochemistry Analyzer, Automated Artificial Intelligence Microscopy, Fecal Analyzer, Urine Analyzer, Digital Radiography unit, Electrocardiography, Color doppler Ultrasonography, Endoscopy unit & Tonometry device. Whether you are renovating your existing facility or building a new facility, it is a perfect time to invest in cutting-edge medical equipment to continually improve care, and create a positive environment for your team, clients and patients.
Read more about modern and contemporary Vet Hospital we designed for our client Marine Drive Vet Clinic, Vancouver, BC
#### Final Thoughts
At Team Medico, we understand what is important when it comes to designing veterinary practice. Our design team have a wealth of knowledge and experience to share with you regarding intelligent design, clinical layout and what is required in a veterinary environment.
Whether you are building a new clinic or upgrading your current veterinary practice space, there are many design choices that can help you craft a space that will delight clients and keep patients calm and happy. Contact Team Medico for more ideas and to discuss how we can help you with your veterinary clinic.

## What are the Design Solutions for Waiting Rooms?
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/what-are-the-design-solutions-for-waiting-rooms/

Waiting room design is a critical aspect of any medical facility. As the first point of contact for patients, the waiting room reflects the identity and values of the healthcare facility. However, it often receives less attention in the planning process. To create an impactful waiting room, clinic owners and designers should focus on patient flow, comfort, accessibility, privacy, and the integration of modern technology. Thoughtful design can leave a positive first impression and enhance the overall patient experience.
In this blog, we will discuss a few key elements to consider when designing a waiting room that will deliver a great first – and lasting – impression of your clinic.
#### Comfortable Seating
Waiting room design should prioritize comfortable and versatile seating arrangements. Providing options for patients to wait in private areas or family groups enhances their experience. Chairs with arms make it easier for patients to sit and stand, and offering varied chair sizes accommodates bariatric users. All seating should remain within clear view of the reception desk to reassure patients they haven’t been overlooked and ensure staff can quickly respond in case of a health emergency. Thoughtful seating design is key to creating a safe and welcoming environment.
#### Layout & Accessibility
A well-designed clinic layout facilitates smooth patient flow and navigation throughout the facility. To make the most use of the space in your waiting room, you need to start with your layout. Make sure it’s easy to navigate strollers or wheelchairs between the furniture. Waiting rooms must be easily accessible, with self-opening double doors, unobstructed pathways, and tables and chairs with clearance for those with mobility aids. When designing an accessible waiting room, however, there’s more to consider than ADA compliance.
You need to make sure the foot traffic can flow freely around the waiting area and doesn’t bottleneck, which may be even smoother if you have a separate exit to keep traffic moving in one direction. Ensure that examination and consultation rooms are strategically placed helps maintain patient confidentiality and fosters a secure environment.
#### Selecting The Right Decor
Colors: Pay attention to your color choices. The colors of the furniture you choose as well as the colors of your walls and fixtures can have a direct effect on the way patients feel. Colors that inspire calm and tranquility are best for medical offices. Neutral colors evoke feelings of calm and comfort. The wrong color could consciously or subconsciously contribute to feelings of frustration and discomfort. Bolder colors such as red and orange may be too intense for some patients. Save bold colors for accent pieces, like rugs and art. If you wish to keep the white walls, choose furniture pieces that are brightly colored. An inspired choice might be a modular seating system made from turquoise and blue elements.
Lighting: Adjusting the lighting in your waiting area can enhance the comfort of your visitors as well and can set a certain mood. Soft, bright light creates a sense of calm and increases the appeal of items on display, which would be good in a business office setting. Your patients can become uncomfortable and anxious if your lighting is too bright. You can have dimmable or adjustable lights installed or choose standing or table lamps that are softer. The brightness should be closer to your living room at home rather than an operating room.
Artwork: The right artwork can create the right ambiance and offer an opportunity to educate your patients about achieving and maintaining good health. It is also a cost-effective method to revamp or upgrade your dated medical waiting room. Feature walls – colored or patterned – are another great way to give your waiting room a warm, inviting feel. Potted plants, fresh flowers, succulent collections, and tabletop water features are simple ways to bring the natural world into your waiting room.
#### Takeaway
The design of your waiting room may not determine whether patients choose your practice or not, but it will affect their memory of their visit. Creating a healthy, productive, and beautiful waiting room is essential for making patients loyal customers.
Team Medico has extensive experience in designing medical clinics and will provide you with insights on how to make your waiting room work for your practice and patients. Your consultation with us is free. Book now.

## What to Consider When Building a New Dental Practice?
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/what-to-consider-when-building-a-new-dental-practice/

Whether you are starting your first dental practice or moving your established practice into a bigger space, building a new dental practice can seem overwhelming. With careful planning and consideration, you can begin constructing a dental practice that perfectly meets your needs.
Here are some considerations to make as you move forward with the plans and designs for your dental practice.
#### FIND THE RIGHT LOCATION
Choosing the right location is a crucial decision when building a new dental practice. Before finalizing your practice’s location, it’s important to research the area to understand the local demographics. Your location should be accessible, close to your target patients, and within your budget. Avoid areas that are already saturated with practitioners offering the same services. All these factors can influence your potential patient base and revenue stream.
#### KNOW YOUR BUDGET AND HAVE FINANCE AVAILABLE
Starting a dental practice will require an investment of money as well as your time and energy. Knowing your budget and securing a loan is the crucial step. It is important that your clinic designer draws your new practice construction plan with your budget in mind.
There are various costs associated with building a dental clinic so here are some things to consider before you plan your budget and secure financing:
- Site acquisition
- Construction costs
- Equipment costs
The best way to evaluate these costs is to get bids from contractors that understand your local building codes and the demands of a dental practice. Costs are going up significantly so it’s important that you have updated information.
Estimate as best you can for initial costs to get your office up and running, and to sustain day-to-day operating expenses for the first few months. Most importantly, yet also commonly overlooked, anticipate any unexpected costs to ensure there is money available, just in case. When seeking funding for your practice, consider the contingency funds. These extra funds can help cover costs you haven’t thought of or unexpected expenses that arise while you build your new practice. This, again, is where working with a knowledgeable contractor can help.
#### WORK WITH THE RIGHT PARTNER
Before choosing a contractor for your clinic design/build process, make sure your contractor has experience working with dental/medical facilities and has done dental office construction projects in the past. You may not think this has a big impact, and the non-specialized or inexperienced contractor may mean well (and may come in the cheapest), but they will hit unexpected delays and costs due to lack of experience in the industry. So many requirements and layout specifications are dental specific that an industry expert is ready for – whereas these could really throw a wrench in the project for an inexperienced contractor.
Choosing a construction company with right team is not only a wise idea but will also lead to more accurate cost estimates. If your designers have lasting, solid relationships with a range of loyal contractors, they may be able to get you a better, and often set, price. You can also rest assured that the specialist services being carried out within your space, such as plumbing, flooring and painting, are the most reliable and professional, as they have been hand picked. They have been chosen for their experience and expertise in undertaking work specific to dental and medical practice fit outs.
#### FIND THE BEST EQUIPMENT
Furniture, equipment, software, supplies—determining and purchasing all of the things you need for your practice to function can be a lengthy, costly process. Make sure to do your research on dental equipment and technology for the best prices, financing and training. Finding the best provider for all the equipment you need will help a lot with the success of your practice.
#### WRAPPING IT UP
There you have it. There are lots of other things we might’ve skipped, but if you’re serious about setting up your new dental practice, these tips and guidelines should help point you in the right direction. If you are looking for additional help, contact dental clinic experts at Team Medico for a complimentary consultation to discuss your practice construction needs.

## What to Consider when Building a New Optometry Clinic
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/what-to-consider-when-building-a-new-optometry-clinic/

Building a new optometry clinic is a significant endeavour that involves more than just choosing a location and setting up shop. It requires careful consideration of various factors to ensure compliance, functionality, and sustainability. Whether you’re a seasoned optometrist or an entrepreneur venturing into the healthcare sector, understanding the intricacies of this process is crucial. In this blog post, we’ll explore seven essential strategies for building a new optometry clinic, with a focus on British Columbia’s provincial requirements, college guidelines, and the 2024 Building Code Regulations. We’ll also delve into the importance of unique design and the role of community support.
1. Understanding Provincial Requirements in British Columbia
Before you begin construction, it’s imperative to familiarize yourself with the provincial requirements specific to British Columbia. These regulations ensure your clinic operates within legal and safety standards, providing a safe environment for both staff and patients. Key areas to consider include:
Licensing and Permits: Ensure you have all necessary licenses and permits before breaking ground. This includes business licenses, healthcare facility permits, and zoning approvals.
Health and Safety Standards: Adhere to health and safety protocols set by the province to protect patients and employees.
Implementation Tip: Consult with a professional team (like us!) familiar with healthcare regulations in British Columbia to guide you through the application process.
2. Adhering to Provincial College Guidelines
Adhering to guidelines set by the College of Health and Care Professionals of BC (formerly under the College of Optometrists of British Columbia) is crucial in maintaining professional standards and ethical practices. These guidelines cover various aspects of clinic operation, including patient care, record keeping, and staff qualifications.
Patient Care Protocols: Ensure your clinic’s operations align with the college’s standards for patient care, including examination procedures and follow-up practices.
Record Keeping: Implement a robust system for maintaining patient records securely and accurately.
Implementation Tip: Regularly review the college’s updates and guidelines to keep your practice in compliance.
3. Navigating the 2024 Building Code Regulations
The now released 2024 Building Code Regulations introduce new standards for all new constructions, including healthcare facilities; emphasizing accessibility, sustainability, and safety. Understanding these changes is vital for designing a compliant and forward-thinking clinic.
Accessibility Features: Incorporate ramps, wider doorways and hallways, and accessible restrooms to accommodate all patients.
Sustainable Practices: Consider energy-efficient lighting and heating systems to reduce your environmental footprint.
Implementation Tip: Work with an architect experienced in healthcare design (like us!) to integrate these features seamlessly into your clinic’s plans.
4. Designing a Unique and Inviting Space
A unique design can set your clinic apart, providing a welcoming atmosphere that reflects your brand and care philosophy. Consider both aesthetic and functional elements to enhance patient experience.
Interior Design: Choose a design that speaks to who you are. Whether that’s calming colours and comfortable furnishings to create a soothing environment for patients or edgy and bold features to transform your patient’s experience. Consider using local artwork and natural materials in your design, to creating a distinctive and relaxing space that resonates with the community.
Functional Layout: Ensure the layout facilitates efficient patient flow and staff operations.
Implementation Tip: Engage a professional designer to balance aesthetics with functionality.
5. Investing in Advanced Technology and Equipment
Modern optometry clinics benefit from incorporating the latest technology and equipment, enhancing diagnostic capabilities and patient care.
Diagnostic Tools: Equip your clinic with state-of-the-art diagnostic tools to offer comprehensive eye care services.
Patient Management Systems: Implement digital systems for scheduling, billing, and record-keeping to streamline operations.
Implementation Tip: Stay informed about technological advancements in optometry to keep your clinic at the forefront of patient care.
6. Building a Competent and Compassionate Team
The success of your clinic hinges on the quality of your team. Hiring skilled and empathetic staff is essential for delivering exceptional patient care and fostering a positive clinic culture.
Recruitment Strategies: Focus on hiring candidates with both technical skills and a strong commitment to patient care.
Continuous Training: Provide regular training opportunities to keep your team updated on the latest practices and technologies.
Implementation Tip: Create an inclusive and supportive workplace culture to attract and retain top talent.
7. Emphasizing Local Business and Community Support
Building strong ties with local businesses and the community can significantly impact your clinic’s success. Engaging with the community not only boosts your clinic’s visibility but also fosters trust and loyalty among potential patients.
Community Engagement: Participate in local events and collaborate with nearby businesses to build a network of support.
Local Sourcing: Whenever possible, source materials and services from local suppliers to support the regional economy.
Implementation Tip: Develop a community outreach plan to identify partnership opportunities and engage with local organizations. For example; an optometry clinic in Nanaimo regularly hosts free vision screening events at community centres, enhancing its reputation as a caring and engaged local business.
Building a new optometry clinic is a complex but rewarding journey. By understanding and implementing these strategies, you can establish a clinic that not only meets regulatory requirements but also provides exceptional patient care and contributes positively to the community. As you embark on this venture, consider these thought-provoking questions: How will your clinic stand out in a competitive market? In what ways can you foster deeper connections with your community? Your answers to these questions will guide your clinic toward a successful and impactful future.

## What to Look for When Choosing Your Medical Clinic Builder?
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/what-to-look-for-when-choosing-your-medical-clinic-builder/

Whether you are building your first medical clinic or renovating an existing office space, choosing a medical clinic builder is crucial. There is a significant difference between healthcare construction and general construction. The unique nature of healthcare facilities requires specialized knowledge, expertise, and considerations. Contractors experienced in healthcare construction know the extraordinary level of detail involved in successfully planning and executing a project and have developed their own checklists. The design and construction of these are best left in the hands of seasoned contractors with prior experience in healthcare construction services.
Here are the essential things to consider when picking a healthcare construction contractor for any project, be it new construction or renovation:
#### Direct Experience in Healthcare Construction
The contractor you choose should have direct experience in healthcare construction. This specialized experience is crucial because healthcare facilities have unique requirements, regulations, and considerations that differ from other types of construction projects. By choosing a medical clinic builder with direct experience in healthcare construction, you can ensure they possess the expertise to handle the specific challenges and complexities involved in building medical facilities. Make sure the Project Executive, Project Manager, and Construction Superintendent assigned to your project have a proven track record in constructing similar healthcare projects. Their specialized knowledge is essential for delivering a facility that meets healthcare standards.
#### Good Reputation & References
A reputable contractor with a strong track record in building medical facilities indicates their ability to deliver high-quality work and meet the unique requirements of healthcare construction projects.
It is crucial to request references from past clients whom you can directly contact when evaluating a medical clinic construction contractor. Do not rely solely on testimonials published on the contractor’s website. During your conversations with past clients, be sure to cover key aspects such as the contractor’s construction quality, their commitment to safety standards, their communication style and responsiveness, and their ability to meet project deadlines. By asking these detailed questions, you can gain a deeper understanding of the contractor’s capabilities. Additionally, this helps ensure that they align with your expectations for your medical clinic construction project, ultimately giving you greater confidence in your decision.
#### Safety & Compliance with Regulations
Healthcare construction must adhere to specific regulations and codes related to patient safety, infection control, privacy, accessibility, and specialized equipment installation. Ensure that the clinic builder is well-versed in local, regional, and national regulations governing the construction of medical facilities. Compliance with building codes, safety standards, healthcare guidelines, and accessibility requirements is crucial to avoid future legal issues or delays.
#### Licensing and Insurance
You should make certain that your medical construction contractor is completely licensed to perform in your area. You may verify this by requesting a copy of their license in their proposal or qualifying reply. This includes liability insurance, workers’ compensation insurance, and any other relevant coverage.
You may also inquire about their company’s health and safety policy or whether they have a full-time health and safety representative. This is frequently an indication that the organization takes safe work practices seriously and is working to educate its personnel and establish effective safety initiatives.
#### Client-Centric Design and Customization
It is essential to choose a medical clinic builder who prioritizes understanding and accommodating your specific needs and preferences as the client. The contractor should work closely with you, architects, and designers to develop a customized clinic layout and design that optimizes functionality, efficiency, and patient experience. Furthermore, they should consider factors such as patient flow, privacy, infection control, and accessibility requirements. In addition, the contractor should design and construct the clinic with flexibility in mind, allowing for future expansions, technological advancements, and evolving healthcare needs. They should also provide a range of options for materials, finishes, and fixtures that align with your desired aesthetics and functional requirements. Lastly, they should guide you through the selection process, considering factors such as durability, ease of maintenance, and infection control, ensuring that every decision supports the long-term success of your clinic.
#### Post-Construction Support
Inquire about the choosing a medical clinic builder‘s post-construction support services, including warranties and maintenance plans. A reputable contractor should stand behind their work and be available to address any issues or concerns that may arise after completion. Additionally, a reliable contractor should have a responsive customer support system in place. This includes providing a dedicated point of contact for any post-construction inquiries, concerns, or issues. Prompt and effective communication is essential for addressing any potential post-construction needs, ensuring that your clinic operates smoothly long after the project is finished.
#### Final Thoughts
By carefully considering these factors, you can select a medical clinic contractor who is capable of delivering a high-quality facility that meets your specific needs, complies with regulations, and provides a positive experience for both patients and healthcare professionals.

We specialize in all aspects of healthcare construction services. If you have any further questions or want to book a consultation to see what we can offer for your healthcare industry construction project, contact us today!

## Why Infection Control is Important During Healthcare Design & Construction in Canada?
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/why-infection-control-is-important-during-healthcare-design-construction-in-canada/

Incorporating infection control strategies into your practice’s design proves highly effective in mitigating risks and maintaining operational continuity during challenging times. The recent COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of infection control in safeguarding the safety of practitioners, staff, and patients within healthcare practice environments. Implementing some of the latest best practices in the physical healthcare environment can help to minimize their impact—and help to produce the best outcomes for patients, families and staff.
In 2011, in response to safety and cost concerns raised by governments, health care professionals, and the public, the Canadian Standards Association (CSA) created the first edition Z8000 Canadian Health Care Facilities (HCFs) standard. The CSA Z8000 standard offers a comprehensive, Canada wide recognized baseline for the planning, design, and construction of hospitals and other healthcare facilities based on leading research linking better facility design to minimize the risk of infections.
#### Design & Construction Considerations That Reduce Disease Transmission
#### Material Selection
Materials that have antimicrobial properties such as copper alloys used for high-touch surfaces (e.g., door handles and bed rails). Copper and its alloys, such as brass, bronze and copper-nickel, are inherently antimicrobial. When cleaned regularly, frequently touched surfaces manufactured from uncoated copper alloy materials will continuously kill bacteria that cause infections. Using copper alloys for high-touch surfaces such as door handles and bed rails can reduce infection transmission. Any material or finish used in a healthcare setting should be nonporous and nonreactive when exposed to common disinfectants such as bleach, alcohol, and ammonium compounds.
Minimizing direct contact with door handles, faucets, receptacles, sinks, and various equipment is another preventative measure for infection transmission. Use of no touch entryways and sinks with motion sensors can remove some common avenues of transmission.
#### Traffic Flow
To manage patient flow while prioritizing infection control, strategies include restricting the number of entrances and ensuring sufficient social distancing space in waiting areas, corridors, hallways, and stairwells. Minimizing exposure to others at check-in desks, ER rooms, outpatient clinics, waiting areas, and other common points of contact helps everyone reduce their risks of infection.
Physical barriers such as single-patient rooms (and separate washrooms in the exceptional cases where a room is shared) as per CSA Z8000. Containing a patient within a private room minimizes opportunities for the spread of infection to the individual and other parts of the facility.
Hand-hygiene infrastructure that promotes hand-hygiene compliance through clearly visible sinks and gels in convenient and standardized locations.
Research demonstrates that sunlight effectively eliminates certain types of microbes, especially bacteria. Additionally, access to natural light has the added benefit of uplifting the moods of both patients and staff.
#### Ventilation
Ventilation in health care is the process of exchanging indoor air with outdoor air to improve the quality of indoor air. Ventilation also helps to regulate the humidity levels in indoor air, which can affect indoor air quality. High humidity levels can lead to the growth of mold, mildew, and other fungi, which can cause respiratory problems and allergic reactions. Effective ventilation not only eliminates odors but also sustains a refreshing indoor atmosphere.
#### Adequate Hand Wash/Sanitizer Stations
Placing hand wash stations or hand sanitizer dispensers at doors and entrances as well as inside treatment rooms near beds can encourage staff to use them on a more frequent basis. Washing hands more often and using alcohol-based hand sanitizers can prevent the spread of respiratory and diarrheal infections. Report shows that compliance to Z8000 requirements related to hand hygiene sinks and alcohol-based hand rub stations increased dramatically after the change in hospital design. For intensive care units in those healthcare facilities, hand hygiene sink compliance rose from 31 per cent to 90 per cent, with alcohol-based hand rub station compliance increasing from 57 per cent to 85 per cent. For the medical/surgical units of those healthcare facilities, hand hygiene sink compliance increased from 40 per cent to 84 per cent, while alcohol-based hand rub station compliance increased from 66 per cent to 82 per cent.
#### Conclusion
As humans evolve, our healthcare facilities must evolve in tandem to meet our changing needs. These considerations are just a snapshot of how the design & construction of a healthcare facility can help minimize the spread of infections and disease. Of course, hiring a qualified builder that specialize in healthcare and particularly in CSA Z8000 compliance can ensure regulatory compliance and make sure healthcare workers are equipped with the tools and environment they need to maintain patient safety and their own.
If you are searching for a dependable and experienced healthcare construction contractor in Greater Vancouver and nearby Vancouver Island area, look no further than Team Medico. We specialize in all aspects of healthcare construction services. If you have any further questions or want to book a consultation to see what we can offer for your healthcare industry construction project, contact us today!

Physio; Surrey, BC; 2,345 sq ft; Modern & contemporary design

Legend Physiotherapy and Wellness has one goal in mind, to help you on your road to a pain-free life. With this in mind, we built a simple yet modern space that would allow patients to focus on their health and wellness-related goals. Our team made use of an effective floorplan and neutral colors from the reception area all the way to the treatment rooms in order to create a space that maximized efficiency for both staff and patients.

## EPIC Veterinary Hospital, Richmond, BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/epic-veterinary-hospital-richmond-bc/
Veterinary; Richmond, BC; 3,300 sq ft; Modern & contemporary design

E.P.I.C veterinary hospital is a 3,300 sq. ft. clinic located in Richmond, BC. A modern and contemporary look was achieved through the use of neutral colors and a simplistic design. Choosing the right flooring was a very important part of creating the perfect environment for any animal care facility. Epoxy flooring was used throughout the clinic for its non-absorbent and impermeable abilities, as well as its high durability and resistance to chemical cleaning and daily wear and tear. The cat condo was truly a highlight of this clinic, with a touch or personalization to make both animals and their owners feel more comfortable in the space. Overall, the clinic is equipped with exam rooms, scrub rooms, treatment rooms, staff rooms, a cat condo and so much more. It contains everything that a veterinary hospital should have to be truly epic!

## Delta Eye Care, Delta BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/delta-eye-care-delta-bc/
Optometry Clinic; Delta, BC; 700 sq ft; Clean modern design

This 700 sqft. clinic is very narrow in design, which meant our team had to maximize space through a thoughtful design process with patient flow being of utmost importance. The millwork throughout was truly a highlight of the clinic space. Both doctors wanted to emphasize optical displays for the retail aspect of the clinic, as well as the front reception area. With a clean modern design and soft wooden tones, this clinic is warm and inviting for patients but also designed in a way to maximize staff efficiency. No project is too big or too small for our team to take on, and both doctors were an absolute pleasure to work with during the renovation design and build.

Located in beautiful downtown Victoria, Babylon Health clinic is our second partnership with Babylon by TELUS. As specialized contractors, a key focus was to create a space that is soothing, positive and stress-reducing. Biophilic design features were translated into the space through millwork design, cedar accents, specialized lighting and its amazing living wall feature.

## City Centre Optical, Surrey BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/city-centre-optical/
Optometry Clinic; Surrey, BC; 800 sq ft; Clean minimalistic design

With a focus on function and simplicity, City Centre Optical is an 800 sq. ft. clinic which includes a dispensary with the capability of holding over 700 frames. Specialized millwork allowed our team to not only maximize space, but create an efficient patient flow from the examination room to the retail area. With its combination of minimal lines, neutral colours and mixed metals, this Surrey optical clinic is the epitome of modern and upscale design. Sections of wood against accents of marble and metal hardware create visual texture and provide a consistent colour scheme; this is visible throughout as you view the wood-patterned vinyl plank floors and millwork paired with gold decorative lighting fixtures and marble countertops.

## Coastal Care Pharmacy, Surrey BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/coastal-care-pharmacy/
Pharmacy; Surrey, BC; 1,950 sq ft

Coastal Care Pharmacy was designed and built with productivity in mind. It is an 1,800 sq. ft. full-service pharmacy with an equipped lab, staff area, accessible washrooms and several compounding rooms. It’s functional floor plan and task specific areas allows for increased productivity for staff members. The importance of space optimization is highlighted by the custom millwork and cabinetry throughout the pharmacy. From initial reviews of municipal building code requirements to the pharmacy design and fixture layout itself, Medico was able to execute and construct a productive and efficient space for healing.

## Axis Primary Care, Surrey BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/axis-primary-care/
Medical Clinic; Surrey, BC; 3,750 sq ft; Modern contemporary design

As part of government initiatives to transform B.C.’s health-care system, Axis Primary Care..
Axis Primary Care is the first nurse practitioner care clinic to open up in the Lower Mainland. The goal was to create a modern, welcoming environment with a focus on high-quality and comprehensive health care. Custom millwork was used throughout the clinic to support the technical medical clinic and storage requirements. The focus while designing this space was on optimizing space and maximizing patient flow, with 14 exam rooms, 8 offices, a boardroom, and a large waiting area Medico was able to successfully deliver this.

## Pure Integrative Pharmacy, Victoria BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/pure-integrative-pharmacy/
Pharmacy; Victoria, BC; 1,950 sq ft; Clean & functional design

This being our team’s second project with Pure Pharmacy, we were familiar with the need for a functional design that maintains a sense of modernity. With this build, our key focus was on building task-specific areas, not only does this allow for an increase in productivity, but it also maximizes product placement for pharmacy shelving within the retail area. Elements such as specialized lighting and millwork are seen throughout the displays, fixtures, and the reception area which were strategically placed to help facilitate patient flow and deliver a better customer experience overall. Finally, to ensure safety, custom security shutters for the dispensary and compounding were wall-integrated for added protection.

## Vancouver Optometry Clinic, Vancouver BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/vancouver-optometry/
Optometry Clinic; Vancouver, BC; 900 sq ft; Contemporary modern design

This clinic is 900 sq. ft. and includes a beautiful 500 sq. ft. dispensary, two full eye exam lanes, a pretest room and a shared lab with a staff area. The dispensary has the capacity to hold over 1,000 frames. Team Medico’s millwork team specializes in using creativity to construct millwork that maximizes the number of frames each clinic can hold. The glass eyewear displays are placed in front of the large windows to expose the frames to bystanders walking by in a way that does not compromise the security of the product. The reception desk is wrapped in neutral-colored tile that sets a warm ambiance throughout the entire clinic, to tie the look together the lighting fixtures were all imported to enhance and maximize the amount of lighting in the clinic.

## Nanaimo Optometry, Nanaimo BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/nanaimo-optometry/
Optometry Clinic; Nanaimo, BC; 2,680 sq ft; Urban contemporary design

The Optometry clinic includes a 1,000 sq. ft. dispensary that can hold over 2,500 frames. It is equipped with two full labs, three exam lanes, and two pretest rooms. Beyond functionality, our team ensured the visual aspects of the clinic were sleek and modern. Designed with light colored walls and flooring the space was refined and given a contemporary look that contrasts the chocolate brown cabinetry and reception desk. There is a half-accessible washroom on the main floor and a full washroom with a shower on the upper floor. The office contains everything a clinic could need and more!

## Surrey Eye Care, Surrey BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/surrey-eye-care/
Optometry Clinic; Surrey, BC; 1,650 sq ft; Space optimization

This traditionally designed Ophthalmology clinic constructed and designed by Team Medico is located steps away from Surrey Memorial Hospital in Surrey, BC. This clinic is 1,650 sq. ft in size. This Ophthalmology clinic specializes in patient care for children; therefore, the design was done with that in consideration. This Ophthalmology clinic includes seven exam lanes, a 63sqft children’s play area and a 180sqft waiting area for parents. Special toys were installed in each of the exam lanes for the children. These toys required custom electrical work that Team Medico had a pleasure of installing. Special wallpaper and glass were installed throughout the clinic to enhance the traditional look and feel.

## Colebrook Eye Clinic, Surrey BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/colebrook-eye-clinic/

## Vancouver Veterinary, Vancouver BC
URL: https://www.medicoconstruction.com/portfolio-2/vancouver-veterinary/
Veterinary; Vancouver, BC; 1,500 sq ft; Clean design principles

This 1,500 sq ft Veterinary clinic was given a total facelift renovation by Team Medico. New ceiling, flooring, millwork, and paint were done to give it a fresh new feeling. Because of how busy the clinic is all construction had to take place after hours.
